name: Retail
blurb: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation at volume, with NRF, Coresight, and IHL tracking the deployments.

points.desc: The Census BTOS series reports AI use for retail trade alongside every other sector, updated fortnightly.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The National Retail Federation covers store automation, inventory computer vision, and customer-experience software - the trade body's research is where retail AI adoption gets counted.
points.name: NRF tracks store technology

summary: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation are the volume use cases.

analysis.body:
The Census BTOS series, updated fortnightly and first asked in September 2023, puts AI use among retail trade firms (NAICS 44-45) at 15.5% in the latest reading, up from 15.2% in the prior period. The figure is the share of firms answering yes to whether the business used AI in the last two weeks. Coresight Research, which focuses on retail and technology and has deep expertise in China, runs an invite-only forum exploring AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-focused businesses.

IHL Group's coverage shows AI deployed across store operations, pricing, and delivery. GE Appliances is using autonomous vehicles, robotics, AI cameras and sensors, and its Brilliant Factory data platform at a Georgia plant to detect defects, predict equipment failures, optimize staffing and forecast demand. Nature's Emporium has partnered with Retailgrid to integrate daily sales data, model demand and price elasticity, and track four natural-products competitors plus Amazon.ca, beginning with supplements. Rainbow's upgraded Shenzhen supermarket uses 17,000 IoT devices, NexConnect Smart Carts, Nebular Ultra ESLs, AI vision, robotics and retail AI for navigation, fulfilment, shelf execution and replenishment. NRF states that digital pricing tools provide greater efficiency and accuracy in pricing.

On where money concentrates, IHL Group finds most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first. Its 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, in cooperation with Chain Store Age, finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. IHL also reports inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion, but empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion, which frames why inventory visibility tools matter.

The clearest retail ROI evidence in the excerpts comes from Dr. Squatch, which uses AfterShip's AI-powered estimated delivery dates and AfterShip Intelligence on tracking pages. The brand achieved a 31.89% recommendation click-through rate, attributed $32,978 in Q1 revenue, cut WISMO inquiries 25%, and reached 94% delivery-date accuracy. GE Appliances reports its tools help cut downtime and reduce scrap, though no percentages are given for those gains.

On risk and regulation, NRF notes that lawmakers are scrutinizing retail technology, and understanding how retailers use data, discounts and digital pricing tools is critical to informed policymaking. New Jersey's "fair share" law raises health care, compliance and privacy concerns for retailers and other employers. NRF also continues to ask Congress for federal support against organized retail crime, and it maintains a Center for Digital Risk & Innovation.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material suggests starting with inventory data accuracy rather than large AI budgets, since IHL's study ties that accuracy to winning versus lagging. Measured adoption is still modest at 15.5%, but the Dr. Squatch example shows that delivery visibility and recommendation tools can produce measurable click-through, revenue, inquiry-reduction and accuracy gains. Regulatory attention to data and digital pricing is active, so compliance and privacy should be part of any deployment plan.

https://nrf.com/.brief: The National Retail Federation presents itself as an advocate for the people, policies, and ideas that support retail, and it provides news, insights, and industry events. Its featured events include NRF 2027: Retail’s Big Show, the Retail Law Summit, and NRF PROTECT, alongside centers for retail insights, digital risk, sustainability, and small business. According to the CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor powered by Affinity Solutions, retail sales increased again in July, the tenth straight monthly gain. The organization states that digital pricing tools fit today’s fast-moving competitive market and offer greater pricing efficiency and accuracy. NRF also says it focuses on policy issues such as organized retail crime, credit card swipe fees, immigration, and tariffs.

https://coresight.com/.brief: Coresight Research says it delivers data-driven insights centered on retail and technology. It also claims deep expertise in China that it describes as unique in the industry. Additionally, the firm reports leading an invite-only, collaborative forum exploring AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-focused businesses.

https://ihlservices.com/.brief: IHL Group conducts research on retail technology spending and strategy. According to their 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, inventory data accuracy rather than AI budget size determines which specialty retailers succeed, and most retail AI budgets fund the wrong infrastructure layer first. The organisation also reports that inventory distortion has declined to $1.7 trillion, though empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion annually. IHL's analysis finds that the presence of AI does not predict pricing-platform quality among vendors, and retailers should instead evaluate explainability, automation controls, and governance safeguards.
